candidate_reports._comment: Raw e-filed candidate report summaries (backfill start) and 48-hour contribution notices (general-election window opens Oct. 15).

race_notes.S-ME: Democratic nominee Troy Jackson replaced Graham Platner, whose campaign raised $21M through June 30. None of that counts for Jackson: his committee (C00955609) registered after the June 30 cutoff and files its first report Oct. 15. Until then, Maine's Democratic candidate money reads as zero, so the race is left out of split signals.
race_notes.S-SC: Sen. Lindsey Graham died in 2026. Darline Graham, appointed to the seat July 14, is the Republican nominee. Her committee's first report runs only through Aug. 5, so her fundraising here is partial until the Oct. 15 filing.

schedule._comment: Workflow fires at :07 and :37 every hour. These dates decide which firings do work. Edit only to change cadence.

text.coord_banner: Party coordinated spending reported through {date}. Monthly party reports add September on Oct. 20 and Oct. 1-14 on Oct. 22; spending after Oct. 14 isn't disclosed until Dec. 3.
text.cand_banner: Candidate fundraising is reported through {date} for most nominees. Q3 reports (through Sept. 30) are due Oct. 15, pre-general reports Oct. 22; after that only 48-hour notices of $1,000+ contributions (Oct. 15 to Nov. 1).
text.caveat: Spending shows where parties and groups are placing bets, not why. Every number is a sum of FEC filings; nothing here is a forecast.
